official.deadline_note: Two windows remain for support starting from the spring semester 2027: 01.12.26 and 15.02.27, each accepting both new and renewal applications. The earlier Autumn 26 and Spring 27 windows (15.07.26 and 15.09.26) have passed. Notification follows at the end of February 2027 for the 1 December window and the beginning of April 2027 for the 15 February window, with payment at the start of March and April respectively.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 academic year - support starting from the autumn semester 2027
official.status_note: EPFL lists the request for Spring 2027 with new and renewal applications due 01.12.26 and 15.02.27, both after the current date. Applications for the 2025-2026 academic year are closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The fund pays means-tested financial support per academic year for 5 months per semester and a maximum of ten months per year of study; no tuition-coverage statement is published for this fund.

Payment at the start of each semester
Managed by EPFL under the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarship

Be in a difficult financial situation under the EPFL social scholarship criteria
Experiencing an unexpected and sudden change in the social, family or financial situation, or in the circumstances of those responsible for support

Meet the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarship

For students who applied to SBPE, the acknowledgement of that application
selection_criteria: Same subsidiarity test and difficult-financial-situation criteria as the EPFL social scholarship

5 months per semester, a maximum of ten months per year of study

official.application_route: One EPFL application form per academic year with the Hans Wilsdorf box ticked - Geneva-based students are routed here instead of the EPFL social scholarship.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students living in the canton of Geneva. Swiss nationals, C permit holders, refugees and holders of a Swiss secondary education certificate may apply from the CMS; international students need one completed year at EPFL plus successful completion of the first-year cycle.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but delayed: international students qualify only after at least one year at EPFL and successful completion of the first year cycle, and they must be living in the canton of Geneva.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Students of EPFL who live in the canton of Geneva or who have applied to the Geneva cantonal scholarship office (SBPE) must apply through this fund rather than the EPFL social scholarship.
official.duration: Per academic year, 1 or 2 semesters, that is 5 months per semester and a maximum of ten months per year of study; an extension may be requested by submitting a complete application again
official.description: EPFL states that the Hans Wilsdorf fund provides need-based financial support and is managed by EPFL according to the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarships, with students living in the canton of Geneva or who have applied to SBPE directed to this fund.
official.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a private foundation, administered by the university

verification.notes: Eligibility, duration, windows and the requirement to tick the Hans Wilsdorf box were read directly from the EPFL scholarships page, with the matching social-scholarship criteria read from the EPFL social scholarship page. Neither page publishes an award value, so all amount fields remain null.

applicant_utility.summary: This fund exists essentially for Geneva-resident EPFL students: if you live in the canton or have filed with SBPE, this is the form you use instead of the EPFL social scholarship, and ticking the wrong box means reapplying later. International students cannot touch it in their first year - EPFL requires one completed year plus successful completion of the first-year cycle, and it expects any funding gap to have been solved before you arrived. The payments are structured as five months per semester up to ten months a year, arriving at the start of each semester, so budget for a lump rather than a monthly stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An EPFL student living in the canton of Geneva whose finances have genuinely deteriorated - particularly international students past their first-year cycle facing a sudden change at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you live in the canton of Geneva, or file with SBPE first and keep the acknowledgement
Check which EPFL cycle you are in: CMS onwards for Swiss, C permit, refugee and Swiss-certificate holders; one completed year plus first-year cycle for international students
Document the sudden change in circumstances, since EPFL explicitly requires an unexpected and sudden shift rather than a long-standing gap
Exhaust and document other sources first: parental contribution, state grants, loans and loan offers
Tick the Hans Wilsdorf box on the 2026-2027 application form, not the general social scholarship box
common_rejection_risks: Applying because of poor budget planning, which EPFL states it cannot support - funding for the whole course must have been secured before joining
Applying to the EPFL social scholarship instead, which Geneva-resident and SBPE applicants are told not to do
International students applying in year one, before the first-year cycle is complete
Missing the renewal window, since the spring 2027 round takes new and renewal applications on the same two dates
Difficulty arising only from the tripling of tuition fees, which must go to the transitional allowance instead and will be refused here
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Support runs only five months per semester and at most ten months a year, so two months of every year fall outside the scheme. Zurich and Lausanne living costs, flights, and any tuition increase caused by moving from bachelor to master are not addressed by this fund.
document_audit: The single application form carries several foundation checkboxes - the Hans Wilsdorf box must be ticked for the file to be routed to this fund
If you filed with SBPE, the acknowledgement of that application is part of the file
The renewal deadlines are separate from the new-application deadlines, so check the row you actually need in the EPFL table
alerts: Two live windows for spring 2027 support: 1 December 2026 and 15 February 2027, both for new and renewal requests
Notification lands at the end of February 2027 or the beginning of April 2027, with payment at the start of March or April respectively
If a cantonal scholarship is later awarded, money received under this fund must be repaid under the subsidiarity principle
A rejected social-scholarship file can still be re-evaluated for a transitional allowance within a few days if the trigger was the tripling of tuition
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single EPFL application form with the Hans Wilsdorf box ticked, submitted in one of the two windows, assessed against the social-scholarship criteria, then notification and payment at the start of the following semester.
